newsitem.title: LATVIA: VENTSPILS NAFTA BOOKS TO SHOW LOWER CAPITAL.
newsitem.headline: VENTSPILS NAFTA BOOKS TO SHOW LOWER CAPITAL.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said on Wednesday it expects the basic capital of Ventspils Nafta terminal to be recorded at a lower figure for book-keeping reasons.

"The basic capital of the merged Ventspils Nafta terminal and pipeline operator Lasam will be around 170 million lats against the earlier figure of 201 milion lats," Janis Naglis, general manager of the LPA, told a news conference.
"But the price of one share will be higher and thus the state revenue from the sell-off will not be reduced," he added.
"Ownership proportions will also not be affected but the company will become more attractive to investors as its return on capital figure will be higher," Naglis said.
Ventspils Nafta merged with Lasam earlier this month as a part of the terminal's sell-off programme and its capital was estimated to reach 201 million lats.
Coopers and Lybrand is currently evaluating the newly merged company.
"Employees of the company will also be offered shares for vouchers for the same price as all other investors," Naglis said.
"This is the first time in the Latvian privatisation history employees will pay a higher price than the nominal value," he added.
The LPA said the merger agreement between Lasam and Ventspils nafta could be signed during the first half of July, allowing the first public offer stage to go ahead around August 20 as planned.
